issues.title: POS price integrity is client-trusted (no pricing engine)
issues.description: POS recomputes nothing server-side for price; unit price / totals / discounts from the client are trusted at the counter. The runtime trades the CQRS/pricing machinery of the rest of the platform for counter simplicity, concentrating risk in price integrity.
issues.recommendation: Introduce a server-side pricing authority invoked at POS sale commit (recompute totals from current SQL product/variant/customer/promotion state, reject client totals like Storefront/CommerceHub do).
issues.evidence: "price integrity is client-trusted (no pricing engine in POS) … one of the top follow-up items"

issues.title: No server-side POS cart (no hold/resume/recovery)
issues.description: POS has no server-side cart; there is no hold/resume/recovery or crash-recovery path for an in-progress sale. A crash/lost-session loses the sale entirely.
issues.recommendation: Add a server-side POS cart aggregate with lease/hold semantics and resume-on-relogin, mirroring Storefront cart recovery.
issues.evidence: "there is no server-side cart (no hold/resume/recovery). Both are the top follow-up items."

issues.title: Tenant `IsActive` vs `Tenant.Status` dual source of truth (split-brain)
issues.description: `Tenant.IsActive` (deprecated bool) coexists with `Tenant.Status` (enum). `TenantsController.SetTenantStatus` writes only `IsActive`; `TenantResolutionMiddleware` gates access on BOTH `IsActive && Status==Active`, so a tenant with `IsActive=true, Status=PendingSetup` still passes. `TenantRegistrationService` and `DevelopmentCommerceHubSeedService` dual-write both. SuperAdmin, Identity, and Merchant docs all flag this independently.
issues.recommendation: Migrate all reads/writes to `Status` as sole signal; remove `IsActive` writes; update `TenantResolutionMiddleware` to gate on `Status` only.
issues.affected modules: Tenant lifecycle, TenantResolutionMiddleware, TenantsController, SuperAdmin governance, Identity authority
issues.evidence: "Concrete split-brain: TenantsController.SetTenantStatus writes only tenant.IsActive … while TenantResolutionMiddleware gates access on both IsActive && Status==Active … a tenant with IsActive=true, Status=PendingSetup still passes"

issues.title: No first-class Subscription / License / FeatureFlag aggregates
issues.description: Verified 0 matches for `GlobalCategory`, `GlobalBrand`, `Subscription`, `License` entities. Subscription/licensing/feature-flag state is implicit in the generic `SystemSetting` KV table or tenant fields — fragile and unverifiable as authority. The brief's assumed governance tables do not exist.
issues.recommendation: Model explicit `Subscription`/`License`/`FeatureFlag` aggregates with outbox events; replace implicit `SystemSetting` hacks.
issues.affected modules: Platform governance, Tenant lifecycle, Feature gating
issues.evidence: "GlobalCategory, GlobalBrand, Subscription, License entities return 0 matches … This is itself documentation/architecture drift: the brief's assumed governance tables do not exist."

issues.title: Projection drift + manual-only repair (no auto-heal)
issues.description: `AdminSyncController` ONE-TIME endpoints fix historical Mongo-vs-PostgreSQL drift (variants in PG not in Mongo). `CommerceHubSearchSyncHealthCheck` detects drift at ratio <0.95 but only *telemeters* (`RecordDriftDiagnostic`); no auto-heal. Event version overflow requires manual intervention.
issues.recommendation: Replace manual ONE-TIME endpoints with scheduled/idle-triggered auto-repair workers; make health-check drift transition into auto-repair.
issues.evidence: "ONE-TIME operations to fix historical data issues … Manual trigger, no automation … drift detected at ratio <0.95 but only telemetered; no auto-heal"

issues.title: Projection version/ordering handling — out-of-order/duplicate replay risk
issues.description: `MassTransitEventPublisher` manually advances `ProjectionMutationVersion` via `IProjectionVersioned`; `IsProjectionVersionManuallyAdvanced` detects hand-bumped versions. Out-of-order/duplicate replay against Mongo/ES vs SQL is possible.
issues.recommendation: Standardize projection freshness guards (version + occurredAt) across all consumers; remove manual version advancement paths.
issues.evidence: "manual ProjectionMutationVersion advancement … IsProjectionVersionManuallyAdvanced detects hand-bumped versions — out-of-order/duplicate replay risk"

issues.title: SuperAdmin mixed responsibilities (governance + finance + vendor payouts in one BC)
issues.description: `SuperAdminMarketplaceGovernanceController` injects `ICommerceHubAutoHealingQueue` + `IEventPublisher` and reaches into CommerceHub ops internals. Finance spans `SuperAdminFinanceController` + `SuperAdminVendorFinanceController` + `SuperAdminCommissionController` + `SuperAdminPayoutsController`.
issues.recommendation: Split governance BC from finance BC; enforce context boundaries; reduce coupling to CommerceHub internals.
issues.evidence: "Mixed responsibilities in SuperAdmin … governance + finance + vendor payouts in one bounded context."

issues.title: Hidden coupling — SuperAdmin → CommerceHub internals
issues.description: `SuperAdminMarketplaceGovernanceController.cs:25` calls `ICommerceHubAutoHealingQueue` directly rather than purely via lifecycle events, bypassing the event-driven boundary.
issues.recommendation: Route through published lifecycle events + consumers; remove direct internal calls.
issues.evidence: "calls ICommerceHubAutoHealingQueue directly rather than purely via lifecycle events."

issues.recommendation: Gate behind environment + authorization policy; remove from production build or strip at compile time.

issues.recommendation: Define one canonical cost authority (e.g. LOT/FIFO or weighted-average) and derive all three reports from it.
issues.evidence: "Three different cost notions coexist … No single cost authority. Priority: High."

issues.title: Cost-field inconsistency across reports
issues.description: Inventory valuation uses `Variant.CostPrice`; purchase-returns uses `Product.PurchasePrice` (marked legacy); ledger COGS posts at invoice unit cost; cost-analysis uses purchase `UnitPrice`. At least three distinct cost columns can disagree.
issues.recommendation: Consolidate to a single cost column/authority; deprecate `Product.PurchasePrice`/`Variant.CostPrice` divergence.
issues.evidence: "At least three distinct cost columns (Variant.CostPrice, Product.PurchasePrice, invoice UnitPrice) can disagree, and Product.PurchasePrice/SalePrice are marked 'legacy'."

issues.title: Revenue computed from two sources
issues.description: Ledger `PosSales` net (Dashboard/reports) vs invoice `SalesInvoiceItems.TotalAmount` for top-products/category. If ledger and invoices diverge, KPI revenue and breakdown revenue disagree.
issues.recommendation: Derive breakdowns from the ledger-aligned revenue where possible, or assert reconciliation in tests.
issues.evidence: "If ledger and invoices ever diverge … KPI revenue and breakdown revenue disagree."

issues.title: Four parallel ledgers with separate write paths (reconciliation risk)
issues.description: `LedgerEntries` (GL), `AccountLedgers` (party), `SupplierTransactions`/`CustomerTransactions` (detail), and `CommerceHubFinancialTransactions` (marketplace) are maintained by independent writers. Party balances reconciled only via manual `RebuildPartyBalanceAsync`; supplier outstanding details read `SupplierTransactions`+`PurchaseInvoices` (a third model) that can drift from `AccountLedgers`.
issues.recommendation: Establish a single canonical GL + one derived party sub-ledger with enforced reconciliation jobs; reduce independent writers.
issues.affected modules: Accounting, Reporting, CommerceHub finance, Party ledger
issues.evidence: "Four parallel ledgers, separate write paths … Party balances are reconciled only via a manual RebuildPartyBalanceAsync … can drift from AccountLedgers. Priority: High."

issues.title: No persisted dashboard/report snapshot (re-aggregate per request)
issues.description: All reporting recomputed per request; no materialized snapshot tables or scheduled pre-computation. Mitigated by `AsNoTracking` + SQL aggregation but re-aggregates full ledger each call.
issues.recommendation: Add scheduled materialized snapshots / Hangfire precompute for heavy dashboards.
issues.evidence: "No persisted dashboard/report snapshot … under load this re-aggregates the full ledger each call."

issues.title: No-op `IMemoryCache` (misleading)

issues.title: No verified export runtime (merchant reporting)

issues.title: Cross-source KPIs (storefront + affiliate)

issues.title: CommerceHub platform overview unreachable from admin controller

issues.title: Affiliate Mongo summary vs SQL ledger two engines disagree
issues.description: Affiliate `summary` (Mongo clicks/orders/earnings/conversion) and SQL-ledger `dashboard`/`earnings-summary` are two engines that can disagree during Mongo projection lag; "earnings" means different things (Mongo daily `Earnings` vs ledger `Earned`); no reconciliation endpoint.

issues.recommendation: Remove hardcoded defaults; require explicit currency (mirror frontend fail-closed).
issues.evidence: "Hardcoded EGP defaults in DTOs … can mask missing-currency bugs on tenant surfaces … CartEvents.Currency default 'USD'."

issues.title: Currency legacy primitive decimal+string (no `Money` VO in order domain)
issues.description: Order/pricing domain uses primitive `decimal Amount` + `string Currency` (re-validated via `FinancialCurrencyGuard`), inconsistent with the `Money` value object in the payment runtime.
issues.recommendation: Refactor Order/Invoice to `Money`.
issues.evidence: "Legacy primitive decimal + string currency in order/pricing domain instead of Money value object."

issues.title: No FX conversion runtime
issues.description: Cross-currency is rejected, never converted. If a non-EGP merchant's CommerceHub payout is needed, no conversion path — only EGP pinning.
issues.recommendation: Design conversion service if multi-currency payout is required.
issues.evidence: "No FX conversion runtime. Cross-currency is rejected, never converted."

issues.title: Currency ES/SQL overlay hardcodes EGP (undocumented second authority)
issues.description: `CommerceHubSearchSqlAuthorityOverlay.cs:204` hardcodes EGP — correct but undocumented as a second EGP authority site; risk if constant renamed.
issues.recommendation: Centralize the EGP constant reference; document all authority sites.
issues.evidence: "ES/SQL overlay hardcodes EGP — correct but undocumented as a second EGP authority site."

issues.title: Currency `CartEvents.Currency` default `"USD"` relies on snapshot override
issues.description: `CartEvents.cs:58` defaults `"USD"` on an event that later hits `RequireMatch`; relies on snapshot override to avoid mismatch.
issues.recommendation: Remove default; populate from authoritative snapshot at publish.
issues.evidence: "CartEvents.Currency default 'USD' … a non-EGP default on an event that later hits RequireMatch; relies on snapshot override."

issues.title: Currency missing DB-level check constraints on CommerceHub financial currency
issues.description: Only app-level `RequireEgpCurrency` guards CommerceHub finance columns; no `CHECK (Currency='EGP')` at DB level. Defense-in-depth gap.
issues.recommendation: Migration adding `CHECK (Currency='EGP')` on finance tables.
issues.affected modules: Currency runtime, CommerceHub finance, DB schema
issues.evidence: "Missing DB-level check constraints on CommerceHub financial currency columns … only app-level RequireEgpCurrency guards."

issues.title: Currency no production parity chaos proof
issues.description: No PostgreSQL-backed mixed-currency chaos proof in production parity; certification is unit/manual only.
issues.recommendation: Add scheduled SQL/Mongo/ES comparison alerting for non-EGP; mixed-currency chaos tests.
issues.evidence: "No PostgreSQL-backed mixed-currency chaos proof in production parity."

issues.title: New payment runtime disabled by feature flags (defaults false)
issues.description: `PaymentRuntimeFeatureFlags` defaults (`NewPaymentRuntime`, `NewPolicyEngine`, `DualRunPayments`, `ReplayEngine`, `ProviderAdapterV2`) all `false`. The deterministic state-machine code exists and is "authoritative when invoked" but is inactive in production. Documented payment lifecycle = older `PaymentLifecycleService`.
issues.recommendation: Define rollout/validation plan and dual-run validation before activating; document which runtime is live.
issues.evidence: "The new payment runtime exists as deterministic domain code … but is feature-gated by PaymentRuntimeFeatureFlags defaults … default false."

issues.title: Treasury `CashIn`/`CashOut`/`Expense` disabled (hidden behavior)
issues.description: `TreasuryOperationService.RecordExpenseAsync/CashInAsync/CashOutAsync` throw — disabled by design. Docs say "treasury operations journal everything"; the caveat is only in code comments, not user docs.
issues.recommendation: Document the disabled paths in user-facing docs; surface a clear error/UX.
issues.evidence: "TreasuryOperationService.RecordExpenseAsync/CashInAsync/CashOutAsync throw — disabled by design … only in code comments, not in user docs."

issues.title: Cashbox shadow balances obsolete (`CurrentBalance`/`ExpectedBalance`)
issues.description: `Cashbox.CurrentBalance`/`ExpectedBalance` are `[Obsolete]` "shadow balances"; any code/doc relying on them is wrong. Use the ledger account instead.
issues.recommendation: Remove usages; document that ledger is the only cash authority.
issues.evidence: "Cashbox.CurrentBalance/ExpectedBalance are [Obsolete] shadow fields; any code/doc relying on them is wrong."

issues.title: Affiliate commissions global (no `TenantId`, `StoreTenantId` instead)
issues.description: Affiliate commissions are global (no `TenantId`, keyed by `StoreTenantId` — the store that owes). A doc implying "affiliate balance is tenant-scoped" is wrong.
issues.recommendation: Correct any doc that scopes affiliate balance by tenant; document `StoreTenantId` semantics.
issues.evidence: "Affiliate commissions are global (no TenantId, StoreTenantId instead) … a doc implying 'affiliate balance is tenant-scoped' is wrong."

issues.title: Affiliate `CommissionLedger.Paid` does NOT reduce available balance
issues.description: Only `AffiliateBalanceLedger.Withdrawal` reduces available balance; `CommissionLedger.Paid` is a lifecycle flag only. Easy to mis-model in reporting/payout logic.
issues.recommendation: Document the distinction prominently; add a drift-detection signal (`Paid` without matching `Withdrawal` = anomaly).
issues.evidence: "AffiliateCommissionLedger.Paid does NOT reduce available balance; only AffiliateBalanceLedger.Withdrawal does."

issues.title: Outbox critical-type list hand-maintained (drift risk)
issues.description: `AccountingOutboxProcessor._criticalFinancialTruthEventTypes` is hand-maintained. Adding a money-posting event type without registering it risks silent loss on failure.
issues.recommendation: Derive critical types from event interfaces/markers; add a startup assertion that all posting events are registered.
issues.evidence: "Outbox critical-type list is hand-maintained … adding a money event without registering it in _criticalFinancialTruthEventTypes risks silent loss on failure."

issues.title: CommerceHub vendor reconciliation complex/fragile
issues.description: CommerceHub vendor reconciliation depends on per-tenant suspense allocation + hold-release hosted workers (`CommerceHubFinanceReconciliationJob`, `CommerceHubPayoutReconciliationHostedService`). Fragile area; depends on workers running.
issues.recommendation: Harden reconciliation workers; add idempotency/alerting; document recovery SLA.
issues.evidence: "CommerceHub vendor reconciliation is complex … a fragile area; depends on hosted workers running."

issues.title: Order projection `Total` vs SQL `Total` no runtime invariant
issues.description: No code computes or asserts `OrderDocument.Total == SQL Order.Total`. Only the 30s reconciliation sweep + on-demand `Ensure*Projected` converge; no compile-time/runtime invariant enforces projection total == SQL total. Event-path bug could drift silently.
issues.recommendation: Add a convergence test / checksum on `Total` for storefront orders (mirroring CommerceHub doc checksum).
issues.evidence: "No compile-time or runtime invariant enforces projection total == SQL total."

issues.title: Storefront `orders` doc has no checksum (only CommerceHub doc has)
issues.description: Only `CommerceHubOrderProjectionChecksum.Compute` exists; storefront `OrderDocument` has no checksum. Repair relies on `ComputeAuthorityFingerprint` JSON equality that excludes freshness fields, so two docs with same business state but different event versions re-upsert.
issues.recommendation: Add a storefront projection checksum for integrity verification.
issues.evidence: "Storefront orders doc has no checksum; only CommerceHub doc has one."

issues.title: Commission double-source edge race (event vs SQL repair)
issues.description: `OrderDocument.AffiliateCommissionAmount` set both by `AffiliateCommissionEarnedEvent` projection AND by SQL-authority snapshot on repair. Repair path uses whole-doc `BuildFreshnessGuard` (not commission facet); a stale repair could reset commission if its `sourceVersion` > doc's `LastEventVersion`.
issues.recommendation: Use commission-facet freshness guard on repair path; add race test.
issues.evidence: "potential edge race where a stale repair could reset commission if its sourceVersion > doc's LastEventVersion."

issues.title: Marketplace read model lingers after storefront order tombstone
issues.description: `MarketplaceOrderReadModelProjectionService.RebuildAsync` returns `NotFound` if the storefront Order is deleted/soft-deleted, and the marketplace doc is NOT auto-deleted (unlike product/homepage paths which tombstone). Marketplace order read model can linger after storefront order tombstone.
issues.recommendation: Tombstone/delete the marketplace read model on storefront order deletion.
issues.evidence: "if a storefront Order is deleted … the marketplace doc is NOT auto-deleted … Divergence."

issues.title: Tenant lifecycle has three owners, no coordinator
issues.description: `TenantsController` (SuperAdmin) PATCHes `Tenant.IsActive`; `TenantRegistrationService` (Platform) controls `Status`; `ServiceDiscoveryProjectionConsumer` reads governance `Status` to derive vendor servability. Three owners of one concept, no single lifecycle service coordinating them.
issues.recommendation: Introduce a single `TenantLifecycleService` as the sole mutation authority.
issues.evidence: "Three owners of one concept, no single lifecycle service coordinating them."

issues.title: Mongo/ES vs SQL projection counts can diverge (diagnostics only)
issues.description: Search/projection counts can diverge; surfaced as diagnostics gap, repaired manually via reindex. `SearchIndexStatus` is the only signal; no automated convergence alerting.
issues.recommendation: Add automated drift alerting + auto-repair triggers on threshold breach.
issues.evidence: "Mongo/ES vs SQL: search/projection counts can diverge; surfaced as a diagnostics gap, repaired manually via reindex."

issues.title: Currency production-parity scanner absent
issues.description: No scheduled SQL/Mongo/ES comparison alerting for non-EGP currency leakage in production. Manual cert only.
issues.recommendation: Add a production parity currency scanner job.
issues.evidence: "Production parity currency scanner — Manual cert … Catch drift."

issues.title: Duplicate currency formatting logic (backend vs frontend drift)
issues.description: Backend `ResolveDisplayCurrencySymbol` and frontend `currency.ts` symbol maps can drift; EGP symbol differs (`E£` backend vs `EGP ` frontend).
issues.recommendation: Single source of symbol map (shared contract); CI check.
issues.evidence: "Duplicate formatting logic … EGP symbol differs (E£ backend vs EGP frontend)."

issues.title: Manual financial repair is a dangerous primitive
issues.description: Direct SQL/bulk mutation, full Mongo replace, raw ES writes, global repair all require reviewed boundaries; drift here can corrupt ledger truth. (Explicitly flagged in `.ai-context`.)
issues.recommendation: Enforce reviewed/runbook-gated boundaries; audit all dangerous primitives.
issues.evidence: "Manual financial repair is a dangerous primitive … drift here can corrupt ledger truth."

issues.title: Settlement header denormalized (`OrderCount`) vs live lineage
issues.description: `PaymentSettlementBatch.OrderCount` is denormalized; posting now requires live `PaymentSettlementOrders` lineage (`SettlementOrderLineageMismatch` telemetry). Docs that trust the header alone are wrong.
issues.recommendation: Treat header as metadata only; enforce live lineage on posting.
issues.evidence: "Settlement header drift: PaymentSettlementBatch.OrderCount is denormalized; posting now requires live PaymentSettlementOrders lineage."

issues.title: Legacy shadow fields trap (`PaymentStatus.Paid`, `Cashbox.CurrentBalance`)
issues.description: `PaymentStatus.Paid` is `[Obsolete]` → maps to `Collected`; `Cashbox.CurrentBalance`/`ExpectedBalance` obsolete. Both remain in the model as traps for new code.
issues.recommendation: Remove or clearly obsolete-guard usages; add analyzers.
issues.evidence: "Legacy shadow fields (Cashbox.CurrentBalance, PaymentStatus.Paid) remain in the model — a trap for new code."

issues.title: WhatsApp transactional-bypass type list string-fragile
issues.description: Cooldown bypass compares against hardcoded `{ORDER_CONFIRMATION, SHIPMENT_*}` list with ad-hoc underscore normalization, while message types elsewhere are `OTP`, `OrderConfirmation`, `PAYMENTAPPROVED`, etc. Mismatched naming risks a transactional message being wrongly cooled down.
issues.recommendation: Centralize message-type constants/enums; unify naming.
issues.evidence: "Mismatched naming conventions risk a transactional message being wrongly cooled down."

issues.title: Outbox critical poison kept on 15-min slow-replay; non-critical poison terminal
issues.description: Critical poison (exhausted retries) flagged for operator reconciliation but kept on 15-min slow-replay; non-critical poison is terminal-marked processed. Operator reconciliation path is manual.
issues.recommendation: Document SLA; add operator dashboard for `RequiresOperatorReconciliation`.
issues.evidence: "sets RequiresOperatorReconciliation on critical poison after MaxRetries=5 … kept on a 15-min slow-replay cadence."

issues.title: SuperAdmin publishes only 7 event types, 0 inbound consumers
issues.description: SuperAdmin is a pure authority writer; verified zero inbound consumers. Intentional, but means no cross-domain event-driven reaction TO SuperAdmin decisions except via direct DbContext writes + outbox.
issues.recommendation: Document the intentional design; consider event-driven notification to peers.
issues.evidence: "publishes only 7 event types … and has 0 inbound consumers … a pure authority writer."

issues.title: SuperAdmin writes peer tables in-process (shared DbContext)
issues.description: SuperAdmin runs in-process against the single shared `ApplicationDbContext` and writes peer tables (`CommerceHubListings`, `UserGovernanceProfiles`, etc.) *directly* rather than via peer contexts over HTTP/gRPC. Powerful but bypasses peer domain services for some mutations.
issues.recommendation: Where possible route through peer domain services / events; restrict direct writes to governance overlays.
issues.evidence: "SuperAdmin runs in-process against the single shared ApplicationDbContext … writes peer tables directly."

issues.title: Reporting cash-flow relies on stringly-typed `SourceType` for cashbox classification
issues.description: Daily Close classifies cashbox/clearing/bank/AR by `SourceType` string (e.g. `SalesInvoice`, `Return`, `Expense`, `PurchaseInvoice`, `SupplierPayment`); a rename silently breaks cash reconciliation. (Overlaps ARC-022 but specifically affects financial cash truth.)
issues.recommendation: Same as ARC-022 — enum + account-code mapping.
issues.evidence: "classification by SourceType string (see debt: stringly-typed source types)."

issues.title: No persisted snapshot tables for financial/operational reports
issues.description: No `KpiSnapshot`/`ReportSnapshot`/`DashboardSnapshot` tables; no scheduled pre-computation (only WhatsApp/Shipping Hangfire jobs). Historical point-in-time re-aggregated per read.
issues.recommendation: Add snapshot tables for heavy historical reports.
issues.evidence: "no persisted snapshot tables … no scheduled pre-computation. Hangfire jobs exist only for WhatsApp and Shipping."

issues.title: Storefront vs merchant revenue account split (PosSales vs EcommerceSales)
issues.description: Merchant revenue reads `AccountCodes.PosSales`; storefront reads `AccountCodes.EcommerceSales`. Two accounts, two code paths; cross-channel consolidation not evidenced in primary reads.
issues.recommendation: Document the split; provide a consolidated revenue view if needed.
issues.evidence: "Two accounts, two code paths; cross-channel consolidation is not evidenced."

issues.title: SOA opening-balance double representation (UI/consistency ambiguity)
issues.description: In `GetStatementOfAccount`, opening-balance transactions appear both in the OpeningBalance card and the paginated list (excluded from Debit/Credit totals only) — acknowledged UI/consistency ambiguity.
issues.recommendation: Clarify the representation; avoid double appearance.
issues.evidence: "acknowledged UI/consistency ambiguity."

issues.title: CommerceHub finance "NetProfit"/"commission" mean different things in platform vs vendor context
issues.description: `CommerceHubFinancialTransaction` computes platform vs vendor partitions; "NetProfit"/"commission" definitions differ between platform (`CommerceHubFinancialTransaction.cs:203-205`) and vendor (`CommerceHubVendorDebtService.cs:333`) contexts, computed via three different methods (ARC-028).
issues.recommendation: Single definition service for commission/net-profit per context.
issues.evidence: "NetProfit/commission mean different things in platform vs vendor context."

issues.title: Identity capability strings returned to SPA are UI hints only, never server-enforced
issues.description: `NavigationCapabilities` (e.g. `super-admin.finance.view`) emitted at login; backend issues them but there is NO server-side `RequireClaim` policy enforcing them (only `Affiliate` role gated). Clients may render actions the server will reject.
issues.recommendation: Either enforce server-side or document explicitly as non-authoritative.
issues.evidence: "The only RequireClaim in the codebase gates the Affiliate role … Server enforcement is exclusively scheme + role-claim + SQL authority + governance gates."

issues.title: Storefront/CommerceHub customer "role" claim is lookup key only, not authority
issues.description: Customer `role=Customer` claim used only as SQL key; no server-enforced permissions. Intentional but must not be mistaken for authorization.
issues.recommendation: Document explicitly in customer-domain guides.
issues.evidence: "customers have no role-claim authority; CustomerId is only a SQL key."

issues.title: Tenant `IsActive` read by interceptor for user revocation while governance keys off `Status`
issues.description: `PrivilegedRefreshTokenRevocationInterceptor` keys user revocation off `IsActive` (`:147`) while governance keys off `Status` — two signals, two code paths, compounding ARC-003 split-brain. A tenant can be `IsActive=true, Status=PendingSetup` and still revoke/validate inconsistently.
issues.recommendation: Unify on `Status` (per ARC-003); remove `IsActive` from revocation logic.
issues.evidence: "interceptor keys off IsActive for user revocation (:147) while governance keys off Status — two signals, two code paths."

issues.title: Affiliate Mongo `summary` (earnings) vs SQL ledger `Earned` — no reconciliation endpoint (detail)
issues.description: Conversion-rate defined twice (Mongo orders/clicks vs SQL ledger `Earned`); "earnings" means different things (Mongo daily `Earnings` vs ledger `Earned` commission). No reconciliation endpoint exists. (Detail expansion of ARC-030.)
issues.recommendation: Single earnings authority (SQL ledger); demote Mongo to display; add reconciliation endpoint.
issues.evidence: "Conversion-rate is defined twice … 'earnings' means different things … no reconciliation endpoint."

issues.title: No automated projection healing (SuperAdmin)
issues.description: SuperAdmin has no automated self-heal; recovery is reindex/replay/manual. `CommerceHubEmergencyStopOptions` is config-only. Contradicts the "repair-on-read/replay" pattern elsewhere.
issues.recommendation: Add scheduled auto-heal for known divergence classes.
issues.evidence: "no automated projection healing; no SuperAdmin notification ownership; no SuperAdmin inbound event consumption."

issues.title: `enableBaileysForAllTenants` DEV endpoint + Playwright default — production exposure
issues.description: Combined with ARC-009 and ARC-038/ARC-049: a `[DEV ONLY]` endpoint toggles Baileys for all tenants, while the production-default transport selection has no auto-fallback and Playwright is production-fragile. Misconfiguration could route production traffic through the broken Playwright path.
issues.recommendation: Enforce environment gating on the DEV endpoint; default transport selection must be safe in production.
issues.evidence: "DEV ONLY DANGER endpoint … no automatic fallback (Strangler-Fig)."

issues.title: Payment consumers non-blocking swallow masks production incidents
issues.description: WhatsApp payment consumers (and service layer) never rethrow; combined with ARC-045, failures are invisible to monitoring. Operator has no signal when payment notifications systematically fail.
issues.recommendation: Emit failure metrics/alerts; add a dead-letter/health signal for notification delivery.
issues.evidence: "All three events are INonAuthoritativeIntegrationEvent — WhatsApp failures never affect the payment lifecycle … never rethrows."

issues.title: Ghost "Accountant" role in live authorization metadata
issues.description: `AdminCommerceHubFinanceController` and `AdminCommerceHubPaymentsController` declare `[Authorize(Roles="Owner,Admin,Accountant")]`, and `AdminTenantAuthority.TenantActorRoles` includes the literal `"Accountant"`. The `UserRole` enum defines only `Owner/Admin/Manager/Cashier/Warehouse` — there is no `Accountant` value, so the role can never be assigned yet it participates in a live endpoint authorization boundary. This is config/model drift, not dead code.
issues.recommendation: Either add a first-class `Accountant` role (assignment path + tests) or remove the literal from both controller metadata and `AdminTenantAuthority.TenantActorRoles`.
issues.affected modules: POS Admin authorization, CommerceHub finance/payments controllers, `AdminTenantAuthority`
issues.evidence: "`AdminCommerceHubFinanceController` and `AdminCommerceHubPaymentsController` allow `Owner,Admin,Accountant`; `AdminTenantAuthority.TenantActorRoles` also includes `Accountant`, but `UserRole` defines only `Owner`, `Admin`, `Manager`, `Cashier`, and `Warehouse`."

issues.title: Tenant `IsActive` (bool) vs `Tenant.Status` (enum) split-brain
issues.description: Two signals exist for tenant state. `TenantsController.SetTenantStatus` updates only the legacy `IsActive` bool, while `PrivilegedRefreshTokenRevocationInterceptor` keys tenant-user revocation off `IsActive` and governance/super-admin path keys off `Status`. A tenant can be logically active under one signal and not the other, causing inconsistent suspension/revocation behavior.
issues.recommendation: Make `Tenant.Status` the sole signal; remove bool writes; rewrite interceptor and `SetTenantStatus` to mutate `Status`/`DeletedAtUtc` consistently.

issues.evidence: "`SetTenantStatus` updates only the bool; interceptor and governance read different signals. Split-brain risk."

issues.title: No hard tenant deletion path

issues.recommendation: Implement a governed hard-delete/soft-close path with audit + downstream child-row handling, or formally drop the schema columns and interceptor branches.
issues.source documents: platform/identity-runtime-final-architecture.md Technical Debt #4, Implementation Follow-up (Implement tenant hard-delete)
issues.evidence: "`Status=Deleted`/`DeletedAtUtc` schema-present and interceptor branches on them, but no runtime path sets them (debt). Recovery lifecycle spec-defined, unimplemented."

issues.title: Affiliate refresh-token reuse detection missing
issues.description: Storefront refresh rotation detects reuse (`TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED`, `IsRevoked` → revoke all). Affiliate relies only on implicit `ClearRefreshToken()` on logout/reset plus `RefreshTokenExpiryTime` check — there is no explicit replay/reuse detection, creating a refresh-replay gap for the affiliate realm.
issues.recommendation: Add explicit affiliate refresh reuse detection (hash-mismatch → revoke-all + audit event) mirroring the Storefront model.
issues.source documents: platform/identity-runtime-final-architecture.md Technical Debt #10, Implementation Follow-up (Affiliate refresh reuse-detection)
issues.evidence: "Affiliate refresh-token reuse detection missing — unlike Storefront (`TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED`), affiliate relies only on implicit `ClearRefreshToken()` on logout/reset + `RefreshTokenExpiryTime` check; no explicit replay detection (debt)."

issues.title: No MFA implementation across any realm
issues.description: No TOTP/authenticator/WebAuthn MFA exists for POS, SuperAdmin, Storefront, CommerceHub customer, or Affiliate. Phone OTP is single-factor verification, not MFA. This is a maturity/security gap flagged as debt in the IAM architecture (by design per code, worth flagging).

issues.title: No impersonation / temporary-authority ceremony framework

issues.title: POS tenant-admin auth/role changes not centrally audited

issues.title: Storefront `EmailVerified` not enforced at login (diverges from CommerceHub)
issues.description: CommerceHub customer login 403s `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` at token validation; Storefront `OnlineCustomer.EmailVerified` is informational/checkout-scoped only and not gated at login. issues.title: Four realm-specific refresh/revocation mechanisms, no shared abstraction
issues.description: POS (session-binding hash + rotation), Storefront (`OnlineCustomerRefreshTokens.IsRevoked`), CommerceHub customer (jti blacklist), SuperAdmin (`TokenVersion`) each implement revocation differently. issues.title: Capability strings are UI hints, not server-enforced; drift risk

issues.title: Capability computation duplicated across auth services

issues.title: Overlapping customer identity models require canonical reconciliation
issues.description: `OnlineCustomer` (tenant-scoped) and `CommerceHubCustomer` (global) are separate bounded contexts. conflicts.title: CONFLICT: Cross-cutting survey precedence vs ontology precedence
conflicts.conflicting documents: `INDEX.md` "Authority Precedence" (`.ai-context/*` › Domain Guide › `docs/architecture/*` › Source code › README) vs `AUDIT-METHODOLOGY.md` ("IMPLEMENTATION is ALWAYS the source of truth… if documentation and implementation disagree, IMPLEMENTATION WINS")
conflicts.explanation: The Knowledge-Base index places source code *below* documentation and `.ai-context/*`, while the audit methodology (which the accounting audits followed) places implementation *above* documentation. For an agent reasoning about browser/QA behavior these two precedence rules point in opposite directions when doc and code disagree.
conflicts.possible cause: Different documents written for different audiences (navigational index vs audit methodology) without reconciling precedence.
conflicts.recommended resolution: Document a single, explicit precedence rule distinguishing "durable architecture QA truth" (where `.ai-context`/guides win) from "implementation-discrepancy investigation" (where code wins), or merge into one statement.

conflicts.title: CONFLICT: `ARCHETYPE_RELATIONSHIPS.md` says knowledge layer is "future `*KNOWLEDGE.yaml`" but they now exist and violate the layer's own rules
conflicts.conflicting documents: `ARCHETYPE_RELATIONSHIPS.md` §1 ("Knowledge layer — future `*KNOWLEDGE.yaml` … declare only page-specific deltas") vs the existing `browser-knowledge/*.yaml` (monolithic, backend-internal)
conflicts.explanation: The relationship spec anticipated a clean future knowledge layer; the layer now physically exists but does not conform to the described shape, so the document's description of the layer is now inaccurate.
conflicts.possible cause: Layer shipped before its conformance was validated against the spec.
conflicts.recommended resolution: Update the relationship/ontology docs to describe the *actual* YAML shape, or fix the YAMLs (see CONFLICT 1/2).

conflicts.title: CONFLICT: INDEX.md "Authority Precedence" omits the `.ai/hermes/audits/` and `accounts/` trees and the `browser-knowledge` layer entirely
conflicts.conflicting documents: `INDEX.md` (Knowledge Map + reading order covers only 02–08 core guides + systems + certifications) vs actual repo (contains `accounts/`, `browser-knowledge/`, `audits/`, `business-flows/`, `platform/`, `systems/`, `_scratch/`)
conflicts.explanation: The index's reading order and knowledge map do not mention the accounting flow docs, the browser-knowledge YAMLs, or the audit tree. Hermes has no canonical routing instruction telling it these layers exist or which wins when they disagree with a core guide.
conflicts.possible cause: Index predates the accounting/browser-knowledge/audit layers.
conflicts.recommended resolution: Extend INDEX.md and TASK_ROUTING.md to register `accounts/`, `browser-knowledge/`, `business-flows/`, `platform/`, and `audits/` as first-class layers with explicit precedence among them.

conflicts.title: CONFLICT-001: Two in-KB audits disagree on financial-architecture documentation readiness
conflicts.conflicting documents: `audits/ACCOUNTING-ARCHITECTURE-AUDIT.md` (peer-reviewed FINAL VERDICT) vs `audits/financial-completeness-audit.md`
conflicts.explanation: The peer-reviewed accounting audit concludes "No surviving CRITICAL accounting defect ... suitable as an external ERP architecture review input" (with the caveat of governance/reconciliation gaps). The independent completeness audit returns VERDICT: **FAIL** for the canonical `financial-architecture.md`, stating it is incomplete and overbroad and that money can move unexplained. Both live in the same KB and assess the same financial documentation/implementation.
conflicts.possible cause: Different scopes — the accounting audit peer-review corrected overstated payment findings and judged the *double-entry engine*; the completeness audit judged the *canonical financial doc's coverage* of every authority/path. The discrepancy is a scope/labeling mismatch, not necessarily a factual contradiction.
conflicts.recommended resolution: Either (a) explicitly scope the accounting audit as "engine correctness" and the completeness audit as "doc coverage," and state both verdicts side-by-side in INDEX, or (b) complete `financial-architecture.md` per the 16 recommendations and re-score. Do not let agents cite one verdict while ignoring the other.

conflicts.title: CONFLICT-002: "README is STALE" warning vs authoritative system READMEs
conflicts.conflicting documents: `02-architecture.md` / `03-inventory.md` / `04-payments.md` / `05-orders.md` / `06-security-identity.md` ("the README is STALE ... do not trust it") vs `INDEX.md` / `TASK_ROUTING.md` (granting `systems/*/README.md` authoritative system-guide status)
conflicts.explanation: The core guides' blanket "README is STALE" statement refers to the PointOfSale repository top-level README, but the word "README" is also the exact filename of the authoritative `systems/*/README.md` system guides. A reader following the core guides can distrust the very system guides the INDEX declares authoritative.
conflicts.possible cause: Terminology collision; the core guides were written before/independent of the `systems/` README convention and never qualified which README they meant.
conflicts.recommended resolution: Replace every "the README" with "the repository top-level README (distinct from the authoritative `systems/<name>/README.md` system guides)" and add a one-line clarification in INDEX.

conflicts.title: CONFLICT-003: Party sub-ledger is either a secondary note or a primary authority, depending on the doc
conflicts.conflicting documents: `02-architecture.md` + `audits/ACCOUNTING-ARCHITECTURE-AUDIT.md` (GL/`FinancialPostingService` as the authoritative model, party sub-ledger as a light secondary note) vs `audits/financial-completeness-audit.md` (party `AccountLedger`/`LedgerService` is a live first-class financial authority that, undocumented, makes the canonical doc FAIL)
conflicts.explanation: The architecture-centric docs frame the GL as the single truth and mention the party sub-ledger only parenthetically. The completeness audit treats the same sub-ledger as a co-equal authority that must be fully documented; its absence is scored as a documentation failure. The two positions disagree on whether the dual-ledger is a primary architecture that requires first-class documentation.
conflicts.possible cause: `02-architecture.md` predates the detailed financial audits; the completeness audit (later, 2026-07-20) surfaced the sub-ledger as material but the core doc was not updated.
conflicts.recommended resolution: Upgrade `02-architecture.md` and GLOSSARY to present the two-tier (GL + party sub-ledger) model explicitly (see DOC-018), and have the completeness audit's recommendations folded into the canonical `financial-architecture.md` (see DOC-011).
